{{also|tion|tìơn}}
==English==
{{rfc|en}}

===Alternative forms===
* {{l|en|-ion}} (as in {{m|en|complexion}})
* {{l|en|-ation}}
* {{l|en|-sion}}
* {{l|en|-ition}} (as in {{m|en|definition}})
* {{l|en|⠰⠝}}

===Etymology===
From rebracketed {{inh|en|enm|-cioun}}, rebracketed borrowing of {{der|en|fro|-tion}}, {{m|fro|-cion}}, borrowed from the stem of {{der|en|la|-tiō}}. The {{inh|en|enm||-cioun}} became {{m|en||-tion}} in Modern English under the influence of the {{cog|frm|-tion}} and original Latin spellings. Always {{m|en|-ate}} or t-final/te-final base + {{m|en|-ion}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/-ʃən/|q2=after a preceding “s”|/-tʃən/}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vealhurl-&#45;tion.wav|a=Southern England}}

===Suffix===
{{en-noun|~|s}}

# {{lb|en|non-productive}} {{n-g|Used to form nouns meaning "the action of (a verb)" or "the result of (a verb)". Words ending in this suffix are almost always derived from a similar Latin word; a few (''e.g''. [[gumption]]) are not derived from Latin and are unrelated to any verb. More often, {{m|en|-ation}} is used.}}
#: {{suffixusex|en|ignore|ignortion}}
#: {{suffixusex|en|scrimp|scrimption}}
